harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «وهو العزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His words «لم»: the lām is a preposition; «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تقولون»; the alif of «ما» was omitted because it is preceded by a preposition; «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause «تقولون», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «كبر» is resumptive; «مقتا» is tamyīz (specification); the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كبر»; and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنْ» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of «كبر».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «صفَّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يقاتلون», and the clause «كأنهم بنيان» is a second ḥāl from the wāw in «يقاتلون».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied verb «اذكر» (remember); the clause «لِمَ تؤذونني» is the answer to the vocative. The clause «وقد تعلمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تؤذونني»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the conditional clause is resumptive; and the clause «والله لا يهدي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The wāw is a conjunction; «إذ» is an adverbial noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إذ» in the previous verse; his words «يا بني»: one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; the preposition phrase «إليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسول»; «مصدقا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسول الله»; the lām in «لما» is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مصدِّقًا»; «بين» is an adverb of place attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); «مبشرا» is a noun conjoined to «مصدقا»; the preposition phrase «برسول» is attached to «مبشِّرا»; the clause «يأتي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; the clause «اسمه أحمد» is a second naʿt of «رسول»; the conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بالبينات» is attached to «جاءهم»; the clause «قالوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ومن أظلم» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; the clause «وهو يُدعى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The object of «يريدون» is omitted, i.e.: they want the invalidation of the Qurʾān in order to extinguish; the clause «والله مُتِمُّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يريدون»; the clause «ولو كره الكافرون» is a ḥāl clause from the pronoun in «مُتِمّ», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it, i.e.: He perfected it and made it prevail; this wāw conjoins to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl for exhaustiveness, i.e.: Allah perfects His light in every state, even in this state.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «ولو كره المشركون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The interrogative clause is resumptive, the answer to the vocative; the clause «تنجيكم» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «تؤمنون» is explicative of «التجارة»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير»; the clause «إن كنتم تعلمون» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «يغفر» is jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if you believe, He will forgive you; «جنات» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: His words «وأخرى»: a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «تحبونها» is a naʿt (adjective); «نصر» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «أخرى»; the preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt of it; and the clause «وبشِّر المؤمنين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, i.e.: We said that to them with a saying like the saying of ʿĪsā; the preposition phrase «إلى الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, i.e.: being, in the sense of turning towards Allah. The clause «قال» is resumptive; the clause «آمنت» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من بني» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «طائفة»; and the clause «أيَّدْنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كفرت».
